record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: What conditions on the stress-energy tensor are sufficient to prove that a static asymptotically flat metric is spherically symmetric, in particular in the conjectural case that a static star is spherically symmetric?

evidence.quote: What conditions on the stress-energy tensor are needed to show that a static, AF metric is necessarily spherically symmetric? For perfect fluid stress-energy, this is the conjecture that a static star is spherically symmetric.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional smooth Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$ that is static and asymptotically flat: there exists a smooth timelike Killing vector field $\xi$ that is hypersurface-orthogonal, and on a spacelike slice orthogonal to $\xi$ the induced Riemannian metric admits coordinates in which it approaches the Euclidean metric and the lapse $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$ tends to $1$ at the standard asymptotic-flatness rate. Suppose $(M,g)$ satisfies the Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)-\tfrac{1}{2}R(g)\,g = 8\pi T$ with a stress-energy tensor $T$ that is invariant under the flow of $\xi$.

Identify natural conditions on $T$ (for example, on its algebraic type, its energy conditions, or its matter model) that are sufficient to conclude that $(M,g)$ is necessarily spherically symmetric, i.e.\ that the isometry group of $(M,g)$ contains a global $SO(3)$ action whose orbits are the topological 2-spheres of symmetry.

In particular, treat the perfect-fluid case: assume $T = (\rho+p)u\otimes u + p\, g$ where $u$ is the unit timelike vector field aligned with $\xi$ on the support of the fluid, and $\rho,p$ are related by a barotropic equation of state $p=p(\rho)$ with $\rho\ge 0$ and the fluid region $\{\rho>0\}$ being a precompact open set (a "star"), the complement being vacuum. Determine the class of equations of state $p(\rho)$ for which every such static asymptotically flat solution must be spherically symmetric.
artifact.status_search_result: The "fluid ball conjecture" — that static asymptotically flat perfect-fluid stars are spherically symmetric — has been established for various restricted classes of equations of state (e.g., results by Masood-ul-Alam, Lindblom, Beig–Simon, and others), but a fully general proof valid for all physically reasonable barotropic equations of state remains open. The broader question of identifying the most general matter conditions guaranteeing spherical symmetry of static asymptotically flat metrics is still unsettled.

status_evidence.title: Proof that static stellar models are spherical
status_evidence.snippet: Static general-relativistic stellar models...are spherically symmetric for physically reasonable equations of state.
status_evidence.claim: Spherical symmetry of static perfect-fluid stars proven under restrictions on the equation of state.

status_evidence.title: On the Asymptotic Behavior of Static Perfect Fluids
status_evidence.snippet: The asymptotic behavior largely depends on the equation of state of the fluid and is still poorly understood.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic and structural questions for static perfect fluids remain partially open.

status_evidence.title: Static spherically symmetric perfect fluid (Wikipedia)
status_evidence.snippet: Model of an isolated star...perfect fluid solution...asymptotically flat vacuum exterior.
status_evidence.claim: Standard framework for static perfect-fluid stars; full conjecture not universally established.
